title: Retailer must approve a return quickly without treating a good customer like a fraudster
job: Accept legitimate returns with low friction while detecting abuse and preserving margin.
trigger: Customer initiates or presents a return.
surfaceComplaint: Returns are expensive, but aggressive rules hurt good customers.
believedCause: Too many customers abuse return policies.
mechanism: A high-volume stream mixes mostly legitimate returns with a smaller fraud/abuse class. Blanket friction damages loyalty; manual review is expensive; cross-channel identities fragment the evidence.

existingSpend.amount: NRF estimates 9% of returns fraudulent in 2025 study

economics.painCostNote: NRF projected US$849.9B in 2025 returns and estimated 9% fraudulent.

buyer.roiLogic: Tiny basis-point improvement on large volume is valuable.

distribution.acquisition: Start in shadow scoring for one category/channel.

experiment.artifactRequest: return outcomes + fraud labels + customer/order history
experiment.success: fraud loss reduction at equal/lower false-positive rate
experiment.kill: identity fragmentation prevents improvement or incumbent already at frontier

claims.text: NRF projected US$849.9B of retail returns in 2025 and estimated 9% were fraudulent.
NRF's 2026 work says fraud tactics evolve across physical and digital channels.
The product question is the margin-versus-customer-friction frontier, not 'block more returns'.
